text:
maria: Quick heads-up — seeing a bunch of flaky failures in the .NET SDK when combining IHttpClientFactory + Polly retries + streaming reads. Happens under load and after a retry: stream is already consumed or request can't be replayed.

jonathan: Ugh, yep that rings a bell. Are we retrying on exceptions only, or also 5xx responses?

maria: Right now the policy covers transient 5xx and HttpRequestException. Policy wraps the entire SendAsync pipeline. We use ResponseHeadersRead for low-latency streaming.

kevin: If you wrap the whole thing, a retry will re-run the request, but if you already read bytes from the response stream before Polly gives up, the original response is partially consumed and not reusable.

sara: Do we stream to the app directly (e.g., return the response stream to caller) or buffer first?

maria: We stream out to the caller. Typical flow: call API, get response, do some streaming JSON parsing from response.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync() and forward chunks to client.

alex: Two quick notes: (1) For streaming endpoints you generally should NOT enable automatic retries that replay the request unless the request is idempotent and you can re-create the content. (2) Use IHttpClientFactory to manage lifetime, avoid new HttpClient per request.

maria: Agreed. I'm debating between (A) disabling retries for streaming endpoints and relying on upstream fallback, or (B) buffer the entire response into memory and let retries be allowed. Buffering defeats the point for large streams.

jonathan: Buffering is expensive. Another pattern: perform the request under a retry policy that only retries on failures before you start consuming the stream (e.g., check status code + headers), then once you get 2xx, read the stream outside the retry wrapper. That requires splitting SendAsync and consumption.

kevin: Example: call SendAsync with HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead inside the policy. Once you get a success code, do NOT wrap the subsequent stream reading in the retry policy. If the read fails mid-stream, you can surface an error but you can't meaningfully retry unless you can resume the stream from the server.

maria: That sounds promising. Can you sketch a code snippet?

kevin: Sure. Roughly:
```csharp
// registration in DI
services.AddHttpClient("streaming")
    .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => new SocketsHttpHandler { PooledConnectionLifetime = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10) })
    .AddPolicyHandler(retryPolicy); // retry only around SendAsync

// usage
var client = _clientFactory.CreateClient("streaming");
using var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, url);
// ensure only headers are awaited so we can decide not to wrap body read in policy
var resp = await client.SendAsync(req, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead, cancellationToken);
resp.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
using var stream = await resp.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(cancellationToken);
// now stream -> parse -> forward; do not re-run policy around this read
```

sara: Also call out IHttpClientFactory benefits: avoids socket exhaustion, handler pooling, and you shouldn't dispose the factory-provided HttpClient on every request. Let DI handle it.

alex: For DI registration + Polly integration example:
```csharp
var retryPolicy = HttpPolicyExtensions
  .HandleTransientHttpError() // 5xx, 408, HttpRequestException
  .WaitAndRetryAsync(3, i => TimeSpan.FromSeconds(Math.Pow(2, i)));

services.AddHttpClient("streaming")
  .AddPolicyHandler(retryPolicy);
```

maria: Good. One wrinkle: some of our requests are POST with non-idempotent bodies. Retrying would replay the body which might be bad. We should have a rule: disable retry for non-idempotent endpoints or require server-side idempotency token.

jonathan: Agreed — either add idempotency keys or do not retry. For streaming downloads (GET), safe to retry if server supports range/resume, otherwise still tricky.

maria: We also saw occasional errors where a pooled connection was reused but the underlying stream read threw ObjectDisposedException after a retry. Sounds like a race with disposing response or cancellation. Any thoughts?

kevin: If you call Dispose on HttpResponseMessage or call response.Content.Dispose while there's active read, you'll hit that. Make sure you only dispose after fully finishing reading and forwarding. Also respect CancellationToken.

sara: CI bot just posted flaky test info earlier — @ci-bot any logs for these failures?

ci-bot: @maria I attached a minimal failing test run: https://ci.internal/runs/12345
Failure pattern: System.ObjectDisposedException at Stream.ReadAsync after retry path triggered in Integration.StreamTests.StreamingLargePayload

maria: Thanks — will dig in. Plan: remove auto-retry for streaming client, add explicit pre-check (headers/status) under retry policy, and add doc comment in SDK: "streaming endpoints have retries disabled by default; use buffered variant if you need automatic retries."

alex: Sounds good. Can you open a PR with code + small test toggling retries? Ping me for review :eyes: @alex

maria: Will do. One more micro-question: any recommended HttpClientHandler flags (e.g., AllowAutoRedirect, MaxConnectionsPerServer) for our streaming clients?

jonathan: Set MaxConnectionsPerServer to a high but sane number for concurrency, and disable automatic decompression if you want raw bytes streaming (or handle decompression explicitly). Keep KeepAlive true (default) so connection pooling works.

maria: Perfect. Thanks all. I'll draft the PR and disable retry for streaming named client. cc: @kevin @sara for tests/integration.

kevin: Thanks — will add a test that simulates partial read + retry to ensure we don't swallow exceptions.

sara: :thumbsup:
